allowed_use: Evidence for the realised sharing of the two operand streams of a grouped MoE launch at the production structure, and for the boundary of the co-resident interference: (1) the weight stream alone realises exactly 2 GSM-group passes (16 passes issued, 8 adjacency groups) at the production point, invariant to k depth, weight layout, resident CTA count, arithmetic intensity and stride pad; (2) the activation stream alone is retained at its short reuse distance (3.0-3.5 passes at the production depth, rising with distance per the cyclic-reuse residency law); (3) the two streams co-resident in one kernel realise 3-6x the sum of their single-stream DRAM bytes, and this interference is NOT a function of launch-physical variables: it moves with resident CTA count (stages axis), with either stream's layout, with the C write, with compute pacing, with the weight row stride's line arithmetic (90-line stride 0.26, 91-line stride 0.39, contiguous 0.10 in one binary) and with the kernel binary's register/instruction shape (52 ST registers 0.41-0.43, 54 ST registers 0.25-0.29, same launch geometry, same machine, same day).
forbidden_use: Any duration. No measured value here may be copied, fitted or interpolated into a Forward predictor or a miss core: the interference magnitude is not determined by launch geometry, so any constant chosen against the production aggregate would be metric-driven selection. The single-stream invariants above are the only transferable quantities.
instrument: mcProfiler perf_exec --custom --per-kernel, host-global serial (one profiler_server per collection, killed afterwards), one numbered per-invocation file per manifest ordinal

geometry.a_stream: gather-dup activations, TOK*TOPK slots over TOK rows, row stride 5760 B, 64 B half-lines per k step
geometry.b_stream: column-block weights, rows spaced N*2 = 11520 B (90 lines) apart, 128 B rows

why_independent_axes: BM/BK/GSM are swept independently (GSM 1-16, K 1440-5760, stages 1-3, work 0-2048, per-stream skip, per-stream layout toggles, weight stride pad 1-8 uint4), which the production cases never separate; the stream-skip controls difference each stream's contribution out of the mix instead of solving for it.
finding: Round 1 (concurrent_phase_sharing_law, synthetic streams) falsified the pure spacing x depth distance law as the carrier of the production deficit. Round 2 (this probe, geometry-faithful streams): each single stream is nearly ideal -- b_only reads exactly 2.00 passes of the 1.06 GiB weight footprint at every depth, layout, resident count, work level and stride pad; a_only reads 3.0/3.5/8.3 passes at K 1440/2880/5760 with the footprint growth the residency law predicts -- while the co-resident base point reads 12.6-14.0 GiB, about 6x the sum of the singles. The interference is destroyed by b_contig (0.103), a_contiguous (0.136), a_scatter_nodup (0.106), no_c_write (0.229), stages 3 (208 resident, 0.102) and work 2048 (0.103), and is unchanged by work 0 (0.413). Round 2b additionally shows the L2 read-request stream is exactly additive across streams (a_only 281.85M + b_only 132.71M = base 414.56M requests) and the interference lives entirely in L2 hit outcomes. Round 3 (stride pad): an aligned +1-line pad on the weight row stride moves the same binary from 0.26 to 0.39 and leaves the single-stream laws untouched; a rebuild adding two ST registers moves the base point from 0.41-0.43 to 0.25-0.29 at identical launch geometry on the same day. An offline LRU replay (phase_spread_replay.c) of the full access sequence at tile and line granularity, lockstep and steady-state phase-spread interleave, lands at or below the lockstep answer (0.03-0.11) and reproduces b_only exactly: no fully-associative LRU ordering expresses the interference. Conclusion: the co-resident interference regime is real and production-relevant (production MoE under-prediction grows monotonically with rows per expert, see experiment_logs/kernel/c500_moe_phase_law/g2_case_direction.json), but its magnitude is controlled below the launch-physical abstraction level (address arithmetic and instruction shape), so no law over launch variables can close it without fitting.

rerun.collect: /opt/mcProfiler-linux/profiler_server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 50123 & /opt/mcProfiler-linux/mcProfiler perf_exec --cmdline "export MACA_PATH=/opt/maca; export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/maca/lib/:/opt/maca/lib:/opt/maca/mxshmem/lib:/opt/maca/ompi/lib:/opt/maca/ucx/lib:/opt/mxdriver/lib:; MIDLAYER_PROBE_PART=<0|1|2|3> <binary>" --casename <name> --output <dir> --host 127.0.0.1 --port 50123 --custom --per-kernel; then kill the profiler_server

build.register_tool: mxcc -resource-usage; occupancy tool: occ_query (mcOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor, 8/4/2 blocks per AP at stages 1/2/3)
